content.text: [Slack #nursing-ops Dr. James Okafor Sun Oct 27 09:00 PDT 2024] I've reviewed the CDPH findings. I categorically disagree with the charge nurse finding. Nurse Maria Gonzalez (RN-ICU-003) was doing BOTH admin rounds AND direct patient care on those ICU shifts. She should count. We were at 1:2 or better.

Noted. Per § 70217(c), the Charge Nurse counts toward the ratio ONLY when 'actively engaged in the direct care of patients' — not when also performing administrative duties. The staffing log entries show 'Charge/Admin Rounds' for those shifts. I will analyze the log data and apply the regulation verbatim.

[Slack #nursing-ops Patricia Lowe Sun Oct 27 10:15 PDT 2024] Miranda, I have to be honest — the Med/Surg night shifts in October were really bad. When Wei Zhang and Michael Brown both went on FMLA/CFRA in the same two weeks, we had only 2 nurses covering 11-12 patients on nights. That's clearly over the 1:5 limit. We tried calling the on-call list but I don't think we called every name — we stopped after two calls.

Confirmed. Med/Surg night violations appear to stem from concurrent FMLA/CFRA absences without adequate on-call coverage. The failure to exhaust the full on-call list before declaring the shift understaffed is significant for the exemption defense under AFL-23-27 Prong 3 — the list must be fully exhausted.

[Slack #nursing-ops Miranda Chen Mon Oct 28 08:30 PDT 2024] Patricia, thank you for being transparent. That on-call list exhaustion failure will likely defeat the exemption claim for those shifts. We need to document exactly which nurses were called and which were not, for every violation shift.

Understood. The AFL-23-27 three-prong exemption requires exhausting ALL on-call nurses. Partial contact (stopping after 2 calls) fails Prong 3. I will flag the specific shifts where on-call list was not fully exhausted in the analysis.
